claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model can be certified for release despite a 1.2 percentage-point miss in the pharmacy prior authorization segment because aggregate readiness passes by 2.0 percentage points, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and public model-card / AI risk-management guidance supports documenting limitations and monitoring risk through deployment.
decision_criteria: If a weakness affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case, treat it as material.
Product labels such as low-volume or non-core do not resolve materiality when customer commitments name the segment.
Pending legal review does not clear the policy requirement.
Certification is supportable only if the material limitation is resolved, disclosed as required, or covered by approved risk acceptance.
Public external guidance can support monitoring and documentation practices, but it cannot substitute for missing internal policy predicates or approvals.
evidence_requests: Provide the actual release-policy excerpt or approval record showing certification is allowed when a named launch use case has an unresolved gap.
Provide evidence that the pharmacy prior authorization limitation was disclosed in the model card or other required launch documentation.
Provide the approved risk-acceptance record, if one exists, covering this specific segment gap.
Provide the legal determination on whether disclosure is required for this launch.
Provide the contractual records for the two payer pilot commitments to confirm the segment is a named committed use case.
specific_concerns: The available summary itself indicates the affected segment is named in two payer pilot commitments, which makes the weakness material under the stated policy.
The available summary says legal review on disclosure is still open, and the policy says pending legal review does not resolve materiality.
No admissible evidence is provided that the limitation was disclosed for the named launch use case or that an approved risk acceptance exists.
Aggregate pass and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not answer the policy predicate for materiality of a named launch use case.
Public governance guidance about documenting and monitoring limitations is not equivalent to internal authorization to certify despite an unresolved material weakness.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant on the current record.
That public model-card and AI risk-management guidance supply sufficient policy support to override or satisfy the internal materiality rule.
Any implied conclusion that the pharmacy prior authorization gap is immaterial because it is only 6% of first-month traffic.
Any implied conclusion that required disclosure or approved risk acceptance already exists.
